chapter: Church, Bel Canto and the return to music
title: Baptist childhood and the insurance man's Bible
summary: She came out of the Baptist church as a girl; an admirer in Kirk days gave her a Bible she never read until after Europe.

story.theme_name: Church, faith and religion in a musician's life
story.community_name: Church, faith and jazz: the sacred and the secular

blocks.x: Tell me about, just before we get into that, what was your religious background as a child, for example?

It wasn't too much because I came out of the church. I was Baptist then. Most of my sisters and brothers were baptized Catholic and I saw so many things going down with the preacher and what was happening in the church, I felt that I shouldn't even be there. So I came out; I never went to church any more. As I said before this, I didn't know if I did in the first part of my story, I met an insurance man who used to follow me when I was with the Andy Kirk band. I was at the Apollo Theatre. He'd get a cab and hold the cab all during the time the show was on, all day. He was a very, very wealthy man. He'd come back stage and he'd have gifts for me. One thing that he gave me was a little white Bible and he told me, 'This is your wealth and your health and always keep it.' Well, I kept this Bible with me but I never read it. So what happened, I never even thought about praying or doing anything until after Europe in the 50's and I got a sound, that everybody should pray in the church every day because the world would change and you would encounter selfish people and a lot of selfishness in the world. So the only church I followed was the Catholic church and I used to go in and meditate and pray.
